clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old boy presented in July 2022 with progressive left leg pain localized to the mid-anterior left thigh, progressing to inability to bear weight and ambulate over several months. Physical examination revealed intact neurovascular status with weakness in knee flexion (4/5) and inability to perform straight leg raise. Initial radiographs of the knee and lower leg showed no fracture or deformity. Repeat radiographs in October 2022 revealed an ill-defined lytic lesion with pseudotrabeculation involving the proximal left femoral diaphysis extending into the femoral neck, with a lucency in the inferior femoral neck consistent with a pathologic fracture. Orthopedic surgery recommended MRI to further characterize the lesion. Pediatric orthopedic surgery performed a biopsy of the cystic lesion, with initial pathology revealing benign-appearing cystic tissue. Permanent pathology confirmed the diagnosis of aneurysmal bone cyst. Hematology/oncology followed the permanent pathology report. Surgical treatment consisted of open reduction and internal fixation with pins and plate for stabilization of the pathologic fracture, curettage of the cyst, and filling of the cystic space with injectable inductive graft and crushed cancellous bone. The patient was discharged on post-operative day one with physical and occupational therapy education for ambulation with a walker.

Surgical treatment consisted of open reduction and internal fixation with pins and plate for stabilization of the pathologic fracture, curettage of the cyst, and filling of the cystic space with injectable inductive graft and crushed cancellous bone. The patient was discharged on post-operative day one with physical and occupational therapy education for ambulation with a walker.
